page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the n4 server family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel core with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It utilizes the x86_64 CPU architecture and includes a dedicated CPU allocation. The processor is equipped with 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, and it does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the n4-standard-2 delivers moderate single-core capabilities but exhibits limitations under multi-core and memory-intensive workloads. In stress-ng single-core CPU testing, the instance achieved a score of 1684.29, placing it in the average tier, which is mirrored by its Geekbench single-core score of 1834.0. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 1714.68 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2251.0. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, recording 19.35 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 12.78 GB/sec for large-block write operations, both falling into the lower performance tier.

The hardware profile includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which support specialized operations like cryptography and integer manipulation. Despite these capabilities, the instance shows weaker results in complex tasks, such as software compilation with clang (2265.0 in Geekbench) and database operations (1259.2 in PassMark). It achieves a static web serving throughput of 4.0 GB/sec and can process 2.43 million Redis SET operations per second.

Given its resource density and performance profile, the n4-standard-2 offers a cost-efficient entry point for lightweight, single-threaded workloads. It is best suited for basic web serving, simple text processing, small-scale development environments, and lightweight background tasks that do not require high memory bandwidth or intensive multi-core processing.
description: The Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-2 is an x86_64 general-purpose instance configured with 2 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, running on a single physical Intel core with dedicated CPU allocation. It features 4.0 GB of memory per core, a 260 MB L3 cache, and advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. While single-core benchmarks like Geekbench (1834.0) and stress-ng (1684.29) show average performance, its multi-core and memory bandwidth capabilities are relatively weak. The instance lacks bundled local storage, GPUs, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses. It is qualitatively positioned as a cost-efficient option for workloads with low resource density. The n4-standard-2 is best suited for lightweight applications, basic web serving, text processing, and small-scale development tasks that do not demand high multi-threaded performance or intensive memory throughput.
